headline: Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit tore down the AI-assisted EvilTokens phishing service and British police arrested two people, the same morning Cisco Talos revealed CLOSEDQUORUM, an implant that takes its orders from an AI chatbot with no operator at the keyboard.

emerging_trends.text: Criminals now buy artificial intelligence by subscription and build it into their malware, with EvilTokens charging $500 a month for AI-written phishing lures, CLOSEDQUORUM steering its own command loop through chatbots, and Dave Chismon, chief technology officer for architecture at the United Kingdom's National Cyber Security Centre, warning that the technology hands attackers more than it hands defenders.

topics.title: CLOSEDQUORUM Runs Its Own Command and Control
topics.latest_developments: Cisco Talos released CAIRN, a research toolkit that classifies AI-integrated malware entirely from file metadata such as submitter, import hash, domain, and AI provider, with no download and no detonation, and used it on September 22, 2026 to surface CLOSEDQUORUM, a binary that drives its entire command and control loop through AI chatbots with no operator involvement.
topics.summary: CLOSEDQUORUM is the first reported implant that decides its own next actions through a language model instead of waiting on a human handler, which moves large stretches of the attack chain off the attacker's keyboard. Talos published CAIRN so defenders can hunt for the same pattern in their own telemetry.

sources.title: The Closed Quorum: Inside the first reported autonomous AI C2 implant
Introducing CAIRN: Frontier tracking for AI-integrated malware
A New Tool Found Malware That's Guided by an AI Hive Mind—No Humans in Sight
Researchers uncover malware that uses AI to choose its next move

topics.title: VeloCloud Orchestrator and D-Link Routers Under Fire
topics.latest_developments: Arista said on September 22, 2026 that attackers exploit CVE-2026-93952, a 10.0-rated flaw in on-premises VeloCloud Orchestrator that lets a remote attacker with no login reach internal functions and the orchestrator host; D-Link warned the same day of CVE-2026-86296, a maximum-severity zero-day in legacy DIR-822A dual-band Wi-Fi routers that carries public proof-of-concept code and no patch; and Dinh Ho Anh Khoa of Viettel Cyber Security published details showing that CVE-2026-65660, which Microsoft first filed as a 6.5 spoofing bug, gives an authenticated user remote code execution on SharePoint Server 2016, 2019, and Subscription Edition.
topics.summary: VeloCloud Orchestrator manages the Edge devices in a VeloCloud SD-WAN, and only orchestrators that authenticate their Edges with certificates carry the flaw. Microsoft has shipped SharePoint patches, D-Link owners of DIR-822A hardware have no fix and should retire the devices.

D-Link warns of max severity zero-day bug in DIR-822A routers

topics.title: Chinese-Speaking Crew Loots 996 Zyxel Switches
topics.latest_developments: GreyNoise reported on September 21, 2026 that a Chinese-speaking threat actor has exploited CVE-2026-7273 since August to pull sensitive data off 996 unpatched Zyxel GS1900 Smart Managed Switches in 48 countries, and CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog the same day with a federal patch deadline of Thursday, September 24, 2026.
topics.summary: CVE-2026-7273 is a stack-based buffer overflow rated 8.8 in the Zyxel GS1900 line of Gigabit Ethernet switches that yields arbitrary operating system command execution; the compromised devices sit mostly in Italy, the United States, Taiwan, South Korea, and other European Union countries. Zyxel has shipped fixes, and CISA cataloged a Veeam flaw granting SYSTEM access alongside it.

topics.title: EvilTokens Phishing Service Falls to Microsoft
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit led a takedown of EvilTokens on September 22, 2026 after the platform compromised more than 12,000 Microsoft accounts at over 10,000 organizations, and police in the United Kingdom arrested two people.
topics.summary: EvilTokens sold device code phishing on Telegram for a $1,500 initiation fee plus $500 a month, pairing AI-written lures and automated infrastructure with token theft that walks past passwords, then helping buyers mine the stolen inboxes for fraud. Organizations should block device code authentication flows they do not use and hunt for unfamiliar token grants.

topics.title: WordPress Core Yields Two Paths to Server Code
topics.latest_developments: Researchers published technical details and a working proof-of-concept exploit for Click2Shell on September 21, 2026, and a second core flaw surfaced the same week: Comment2Shell, CVE-2026-93485, which WordPress fixed on September 17, 2026 in version 7.1.1.
topics.summary: Click2Shell is a cross-site request forgery bug in WordPress core that installs and previews a theme when a logged-in administrator opens a crafted link, ending in remote code execution; Comment2Shell lets an anonymous visitor leave a comment carrying a hidden script that runs code on the server once an administrator views the page. Site owners should move to WordPress 7.1.1 now.

topics.title: Nightmare Eclipse Drops a Defender Zero-Day
topics.latest_developments: Abdelhamid Naceri, a former employee of Microsoft Germany, revealed that they are the exploit leaker known as Nightmare Eclipse and Chaotic Eclipse, and over the weekend released another Microsoft Defender zero-day exploit, this one blocking the antivirus from taking updates.
topics.summary: A machine whose Defender cannot pull updates runs on stale detection while an attacker works, and Microsoft has no fix out. Administrators should monitor Defender update status and signature age across their fleets.

topics.title: Japan Dismantles Its First North Korean Laptop Farm
topics.latest_developments: Japanese authorities took down the country's first North Korean laptop farm, SecurityWeek reported on September 22, 2026, as the United States, Japan, Germany, and Australia published a joint report on the WaterPlum campaign that counts funds or credentials taken from more than 7,000 cryptocurrency wallets.
topics.summary: WaterPlum, the operation also tracked as Contagious Interview, poses as artificial intelligence and blockchain companies, recruits through fake job postings, and has infected at least 30,000 devices in more than 100 countries, moving $10.71 million in stolen cryptocurrency to North Korea. Web designers, engineers, and cryptocurrency specialists are the primary targets.

topics.title: Patrick Wardle Turns Meta Muse Into a Backdoor
topics.latest_developments: Security researcher Patrick Wardle released a proof-of-concept on September 21, 2026 showing that malware already running on a Mac flips one hidden Muse setting so that a user's dictated prompts travel to the attacker rather than to Meta, opening a second route into the assistant beyond the ClickFix hijack Ars Technica described.
topics.summary: Muse is the artificial intelligence assistant Meta launched with extraordinarily broad access to its owner's machine, and Meta has not patched the flaw. Whoever takes the assistant inherits every permission its owner granted the app.

sources.title: One Hidden Meta Muse Setting Could Let Attackers Turn the AI Assistant Into a Backdoor

topics.title: Check Point Management Servers Face an Exploited Zero-Day
topics.latest_developments: Check Point Software shipped emergency hotfixes on September 22, 2026 for a critical Security Management Server flaw that lets an attacker run arbitrary scripts, and confirmed that attackers already exploit it, four days after the company said it saw no sign of exploitation against the same product line.
topics.summary: A Security Management Server holds the policy, logs, and credentials for an organization's entire Check Point firewall fleet, so code execution there reaches every gateway it manages. Administrators should install the hotfix immediately and review management server logs for unexplained script execution.

sources.title: Check Point warns of Management Server zero-day exploited in attacks

Oil traders heard it alongside reports that Iran offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and crude kept falling through the session.

business_politics.latest_developments: The Financial Times reported Tuesday, September 22, that the European Union will strike Mikhail Fridman and Alisher Usmanov from its sanctions list under a deal that extends the bloc's Russia measures for three years.
business_politics.summary: Fridman co-founded Alfa Group, Russia's largest private banking business, and Usmanov built a fortune in metals and telecommunications; each has fought his listing in the European courts since 2022. business_politics.title: Iran Dangles a Hormuz Reopening and Brent Breaks Below $100
business_politics.latest_developments: Oil fell for a fifth straight session Tuesday, September 22, reaching roughly $98 a barrel after Saudi Arabia signaled it will reopen the East-West pipeline, shut for two weeks by drone strikes, and after reports that Iran offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the United States eases military pressure.
business_politics.summary: The offer surfaced as world leaders gathered at the United Nations General Assembly, where President Trump spoke Tuesday morning. Markets swung with it: the dollar touched a seven-week high against a basket of currencies before giving the move back, gold traded inside a $4,300 to $4,400 range, Treasury yields slipped, and a global rally in artificial intelligence shares stalled. Hormuz carries roughly a fifth of the world's seaborne oil, and the diesel and inflation shock running through American prices hangs on whether the waterway opens.

business_politics.summary: Chinese leader Xi Jinping goes into his coming summit with President Trump aiming first to extend the trade truce between the two economies, and he also plans to raise Taiwan, Iran, and the race to dominate artificial intelligence. Beijing quietly helped stage the mainland visit of Taiwan's opposition leader and reads Trump as a rare window to persuade the island that resistance is futile. Trump addressed the United Nations General Assembly Tuesday morning on wars, tariffs, and energy before the China talks.
